hypotheses.root_cause: QoS credits ran out on the NOC0 fabric during a congestion episode on the CPU/PCIe/DDR routes, and the stalled traffic most likely led to the DMA→MMIO transaction 0xB6BA timing out (rc=-62).
hypotheses.rationale: The only catalogue tell-tale anywhere in the run is the QoS-starvation one: at 3.201s, 'QoS credit starvation | initiator=CPU0 credits=0'. It sits inside a congestion episode from 3.153s to 3.531s (txn_q=high, stall_pct 24-34%, on the CPU<->PCIE and PCIE<->DDR routes). There are no deadlock markers ('dependency cycle'/'cycle') and no DMA burst-overflow markers ('burst_len'). The two closest past incidents (run 21, deadlock; run 10, burst overflow) don't match this run's evidence. Three things lower my confidence. (1) The starved initiator was CPU0, but the request that timed out came from DMA. (2) By about 3.83s the queues had drained (txn_q=low, stall 2-6%), so the fabric wasn't congested when the timeout hit at 3.927s. A request stuck since the congestion window, or a slow MMIO target, could explain that. (3) The NOC0 register dump is raw hex with no decode. The PCIe retrain counter went from 34 to 35 at 3.945s, but that was after the timeout, so it's probably a side effect. An unresponsive MMIO/PCIe target (OTHER) is the main alternative.
recommended_actions: Decode the NOC0 register dump (0x60000A86-0x60000AD2) to get the per-initiator credit counters and where txn 0xB6BA was waiting (in the fabric or at the MMIO target)
Re-run with QoS weights/credits rebalanced and age-based arbitration enabled on the CPU<->PCIE and PCIE<->DDR links; check whether both the starvation warnings and the timeout go away
Rule out an unresponsive MMIO target: trace the target of txn 0xB6BA and check its PCIe link state and AER/retrain history around 3.9s
Add per-initiator credit telemetry (DMA as well as CPU0) so the starved initiator can be matched to the one that timed out
